newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS BOURSE SEEN BOUNCY AHEAD FUTURES EXPIRY.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS BOURSE SEEN BOUNCY AHEAD FUTURES EXPIRY.

text.p: Belgian shares are set for another bouncy day on Thursday, dealers said, as the expiry of stock index futures and options will add fuel to an already volatile market.
The Bel-20 index, which fell 2.5 percent intraday on Wednesday to stand 0.46 percent lower at the close, stood 10.49 points or 0.40 percent higher at 2,408.80 after 45 minutes of trading.
"We might see some major swings this afternoon, after the U.S. data come out and when the Bel-20 future expires," one dealer said.
U.S. July CPI, seen up 2.4 percent year-on-year, is due at 1230 GMT.

Dealers said the market's undertone was bearish as many players had started unwinding long positions and turned cautious in general. "We remain fundamentally optimistic but protect ourselves from a possible sell-off by avoiding overpriced growth stocks and by buying undervalued cyclical shares," brokerage Corluy said in a research note.
Blue chip shares moved in narrow ranges. Retailers Colruyt and GIB were up two and 1.5 percent respectively. -- Geert De Clercq +32 2 287 6813
